title: RAW exploratory C0: one nominal light product for ok-aiin and oko-aiin
summary: EXPLORATORY_PARTIAL_NOT_SEMANTICALLY_TESTED. On both whole f68r2 rings and the whole exposed f89v1.13-20 unit, propose ok=MOON, oko=SUN and a single nominal LIGHT_OF(B) constructor only for those bases. Unlike IDEA781 this is not LIGHTS(B,X), consumes no following recipient and yields light attributed to a body without asserting intrinsic lunar emission. All neighbours, ar/or, q/ch and nonmatching wholes remain untranslated. Compare W's fixed-zodiac proper-return interval; neither product is selected without written consumers. No complete sentence or translated word is claimed.

design.mechanism: Two provisional body bases and one nominal externally manifest LIGHT_OF constructor, restricted to their frozen exact host parses.
design.unit: All288 existing Y_COMPLETE_UNITS reader groups: both f68r2 rings and complete f89v1.13-20 unit.
design.contrast: Nominal LIGHT_OF(B), not Y mandatory binary LIGHTS(B,X); W interval product and generic content/property/reference remain rivals.
design.prediction: Exact okoaiin and okaiin have the same nominal constructor with distinct body arguments; no following recipient is consumed. Opaque q/ch wrappers and all differing wholes remain unassigned. Solitary use requires no missing semantic operand, but this does not independently identify light.
design.scope: Partial exploratory authoring on already exposed owned units, no all-prose selection or reserved test. No ar/or rule, no general aiin meaning.

constructor.meaning: Externally manifest light attributed to B; no intrinsic-emission claim or specified recipient.

source_evidence.limit: Normalized later-fifteenth-century Morgan source distinguishes received sunlight from Earth-facing lunar light; no target binding. Historical possibility only.
